Ava / team — quick take after reviewing the redline: 

1) Rollback clause: suggest we accept an operational rollback request from Acme but gate it with a mutual-change confirmation and one-week notice in writing. A unilateral rollback right for the customer without operational constraints exposes Redwood to churn of reserved capacity. Proposed language: "Customer may request a rollback within 30 days of deployment; rollback will be executed subject to a 7-day notice and mutual confirmation of affected deployments." This keeps the change-order model and avoids touching the MSA.

2) Liability / indemnity edits in the redline: Acme attempted to narrow Redwoods liability beyond our standard cap. We should hold to current MSA liability caps; counter their proposed language and offer to add a targeted SLA credit for the Q3 uplift (e.g., token-based credit if latency targets missed) instead of increasing liability.

3) Data residency: agreeable; update the SOW to specify telemetry storage in the US region and include a sentence on retention (e.g., 90 days for debug logs unless longer retention is agreed). No MSA change needed for that ask.

4) Pricing/discount: thats commercial; propose we treat the +15k as a committed uplift billed monthly and offer 7.5% off incremental usage rather than 10% to preserve margin. If sales wants 10%, we should request approval from RevOps.

Recommendation: proceed with a single change order (Order Form + SOW update) rather than MSA amendments. Ill add tracked change suggestions to the OrderForm_ACME_Q3_2027.docx and draft the rollback wording. If Neha needs legal wording for alternate pricing structures, I can insert conditional language.

—Rishi
